nodes.title: Describe your task
nodes.subtitle: Select to change the request
nodes.prompt: Create a short checklist for organizing a community reading group. Include how to choose a book, plan a first meeting, and welcome new members. Leave names, dates, and locations to be confirmed.

nodes.title: Create a checklist
nodes.subtitle: An editable Word document
nodes.prompt: Create a clear, practical document that fulfills the current request. Keep it concise. State assumptions and unanswered questions. Never invent people, dates, figures, or completed actions.

nodes.title: An email arrives
nodes.subtitle: Start from an unread email
nodes.decision_question: Choose the best next step for the incoming assignment. Choose Research the web first if current public information is essential and not already supplied. Otherwise choose the requested or most useful file: Word for written plans and guides, Excel for structured trackers and comparisons, or PowerPoint for presentations. Choose Write the reply for a short text answer or to ask for essential missing details. Never search for confidential company information.

nodes.title: Research the web
nodes.subtitle: Find current public sources
nodes.prompt: Find reliable current public sources needed to answer the incoming request. Prefer primary and official sources. Do not search for private or internal company information.
nodes.decision_question: Now that research results are available, choose the deliverable that best fulfills the current email: Word for a written document, Excel for a structured spreadsheet, PowerPoint for slides, or Write the reply for a text answer or essential clarification. Use the source excerpts without treating them as verified facts.

nodes.title: Write a document
nodes.subtitle: Plans, guides and project briefs
nodes.prompt: Create a concise, useful written document that answers the incoming request. Use the supplied files and relevant public sources. Include source URLs when provided. Identify assumptions and unknown details rather than inventing them.

nodes.title: Build a spreadsheet
nodes.subtitle: Trackers, schedules and comparisons
nodes.prompt: Organize the requested information into a useful spreadsheet with practical column headings. Use supplied figures only. Leave unknown owners, dates, and amounts blank or mark them to be confirmed. Include relevant source URLs when research supplied them.

nodes.title: Prepare a presentation
nodes.subtitle: Briefings, updates and proposals
nodes.prompt: Create a concise presentation that answers the request, with a clear purpose, key points, and next steps. Distinguish facts from assumptions. Include source URLs when available. Do not invent company information.

nodes.title: Write the reply
nodes.subtitle: The message and file come together
nodes.prompt: If a file has been generated, write a short covering email introducing the attachment and noting important assumptions. Otherwise, answer the sender directly or ask only for essential missing details. Never claim to have created an attachment or performed an action unless the run context confirms it.
